We conclude that the apparent failure of the Reproducibility Project to replicate many target effects can be adequately explained by overestimation of effect sizes (or overestimation of evidence against the null hypothesis) due to small sample sizes and publication bias in the psychological literature.

Here, we formally evaluate that insight, and use the results of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology to conclude that publication bias and low-powered designs indeed contribute to the poor reproducibility, but also that many of the replication attempts in OSC were themselves underpowered.
